assessments.reasoning: Chapter 5 explains how imports bring entities into a module's scope and exports make entities available to other modules. Section 5.2 supplies the omitted-list rule. Its default exports locally defined values, types and classes and excludes imports.

challenge.method: Consider a module that imports an entity and omits its export list. Does that entity automatically become available to clients?
challenge.results: The default excludes the imported entity. The two passages support distinct import and export mechanisms and account for an implicit export list.

limitations: An omitted export list has a documented default, so this description does not imply every module spells out an explicit list.
This is a description of the Haskell 2010 module model. It does not claim that all modules have written import or export lists.
